title: Head, Workforce Development
description: THE OPPORTUNITY Reporting to the Director, Country Programs, the Head, Workforce Development will lead the workforce development portfolio within Kenya’s country program, leveraging education, skills development, and the digital economy to expand young people’s access to dignified and fulfilling work. The role will support delivery of the Young Africa Works Country Roadmap through program development, implementation, learning, reporting, and stakeholder management. It requires a visionary leader with a strong understanding of digital trends, a passion for workforce development, and the ability to advance innovation, skill-building, inclusion, and economic growth. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Strategy, program design, and delivery Identify opportunities to create impact through education and skills interventions aligned with the Kenya Country Roadmap. Develop and execute a programmatic approach that creates synergy, strategic coherence, and alignment across education, skilling, school-to-work transitions, and the preparation and placement of young people in work. Set workforce development goals and targets—including internships, fellowships, job placement, entrepreneurship, and further education—and monitor and report on progress, results, and learning. Integrate education and skills initiatives with transitions, youth engagement and inclusion, youth-led grassroots solutions, access to finance, and digital enablement. Provide technical leadership to ensure country programs and partnerships respond to the current and emerging needs of young people, especially young women. Prepare and present regular reports to senior leadership on key performance indicators, program effectiveness, learning, and areas for improvement. Youth engagement and inclusion Establish trusted and accessible forums that enable young people’s networks and groups, especially young women, to contribute to program design and implementation. Support Country Programs colleagues during partnership co-creation to ensure a strong youth lens across education and skilling, access to finance, and digital enablement. Support implementing partners to build effective youth engagement and outreach mechanisms that keep young women and men at the centre of their approach. Drive inclusion by ensuring entrepreneurship and transition programs address the specific constraints faced by young people with different needs. Facilitate innovation and locally led solutions that engage young people and unlock opportunities in emerging economic sectors. Partnerships and stakeholder management Identify collaboration opportunities within the existing partner network and develop new partnerships relevant to Kenya’s context. Manage relationships with senior stakeholders, including educational institutions, mandated public offices, government ministries, private sector actors, and youth-led organizations. Coordinate internal and external meetings involving country program partners on workforce development priorities. Support the timely preparation of workforce development communications for internal and external audiences and approval. Financial management and team leadership Support development of the Workforce Development unit and country program budgets in line with established policies and processes. Coach and mentor colleagues within the Workforce Development unit and across the wider country program. Drive and inspire technical excellence within the team. Lead the team to deliver results in line with Foundation goals and key performance indicators. WHO YOU ARE Master’s degree in Education, Management, Economic Development, or another relevant social sciences field, together with substantial relevant experience. Minimum of 12 years of experience in a similar or related role within a fast-paced environment, including local and multinational experience. Strong operational expertise in education policy and planning, with the ability to lead complex policy and strategy dialogue. Demonstrated leadership and supervisory experience, with an established track record of managing and developing high-performing teams. Proven ability to influence policy and dialogue across sectors without direct control or authority. In-depth experience and a strong record of results working across educational practices, disciplines, and institutional boundaries. Strong partnership management experience involving multiple stakeholders across the public and private sectors. Excellent prioritization, managerial, interpersonal, communication, writing, presentation, critical thinking, and analytical skills. Strong strategic judgement, including the ability to prioritize effectively and exit activities that no longer deliver sufficient value. Flexible, adaptable, and agile, with the ability to manage multiple deadlines and changing priorities. Ability to communicate complex information and data clearly to diverse audiences across cultures. Professional maturity, cultural sensitivity, and impeccable integrity that exemplify the Foundation’s values. Strong commitment to Mastercard Foundation’s values and vision. The Mastercard Foundation values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the organization and we are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Completion of satisfactory business references and background checks are essential conditions of employment. For more information and to sign up for the Foundation’s newsletter, please visit http://www.mastercardfdn.org/ Follow the Foundation on Twitter at MastercardFdn

title: Lead Market Systems Development
description: THE OPPORTUNITY Reporting to the Head, Entrepreneurship Development, the Lead, Market Systems Development plays a crucial role in orchestrating and delivering substantial program initiatives, using leadership skills to unite diverse stakeholders towards impactful outcomes. The role leverages strategic influence and collaboration without direct authority, requiring skilled negotiation, persuasion, and innovative problem-solving. It also requires proficiency in programming, program design, and implementation to ensure that projects align with strategic objectives and are delivered efficiently and effectively. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Program design and management Lead the conceptualization and design of innovative development programs, applying a deep understanding of market systems and stakeholder needs to create scalable and sustainable solutions. Use rigorous data analysis and sector insights to align program designs with local and international development objectives and enable transformative impact. Strategically design, implement, and evaluate large-scale development programs, aligning governmental bodies, NGOs, and private sector partners around common goals through influence and consensus-building. Use persuasive communication and strategic thinking to foster collaboration and oversee planning, monitoring, and stakeholder coordination, ensuring objectives are achieved on time, within budget, and for maximum impact. Stakeholder engagement and negotiation Build and maintain robust relationships with all program stakeholders. Employ expert negotiation skills to resolve conflicts, secure necessary resources, and strengthen program effectiveness. Manage stakeholders and build effective partnerships through influence, persuasion, and collaboration without direct authority. Capacity building and coaching Strengthen the capabilities of partner organizations through systematic coaching, training, and technical assistance. Facilitate the exchange of knowledge and skills to build the consortium’s overall capability and resilience. Impact measurement Implement rigorous methods for tracking, evaluating, and reporting on program progress and outcomes. Use data-driven insights to guide strategic adjustments and promote continuous improvement. Advocacy and representation Represent the Foundation prominently at public forums, conferences, workshops, and other stakeholder engagements. Communicate program benefits effectively and advocate for supportive policies and further investment. WHO YOU ARE Bachelor’s degree in International Development, Business Administration, or a related field. A master’s degree is preferred. Minimum of 12 years of experience leading and managing large-scale development programs, preferably in diverse and dynamic settings. Technical knowledge, or access to relevant expertise, in market systems, resilience concepts, private sector development, and sustainable development in fragile socioeconomic ecosystems. Demonstrated ability to manage stakeholders and build partnerships without direct authority. Strong leadership skills, with the capacity to influence, persuade, and negotiate effectively. Proven expertise in program management, program design and implementation, strategic planning, and organizational dynamics. Strong analytical skills and demonstrated ability to apply systems thinking to complex development challenges. Excellent communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage stakeholders at all levels, including senior government and business leaders. Proactive, driven, and able to work independently and collaboratively as part of a team. High degree of professionalism and integrity, aligned with the Foundation’s values and commitment to quality. Ability to navigate complex environments, promote innovative practices, and foster a culture of continuous improvement. Experience in capacity building, technical assistance, and stakeholder engagement. Fluency in English; proficiency in additional languages is an advantage. The Mastercard Foundation values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the organization and we are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Completion of satisfactory business references and background checks are essential conditions of employment. For more information and to sign up for the Foundation’s newsletter, please visit http://www.mastercardfdn.org/ Follow the Foundation on Twitter at MastercardFdn

title: Head, Inclusion
description: THE OPPORTUNITY Reporting to the Country Director-Senegal, the Head, Gender and Inclusion will provide strategic leadership for gender equality, disability inclusion, refugee and displaced-person inclusion, youth engagement, and safeguarding across the Senegal portfolio and the broader WAEMU Countries. The Senegal portfolio operates through a multi-country approach, with programs designed and implemented to deliver shared strategic outcomes across multiple countries of the WAEMU zone. The role will ensure that the Foundations inclusion ambitions are translated into program design, partner practices, portfolio performance, and measurable outcomes for young people. The successful candidate will work across the portfolio to strengthen inclusive program delivery, promote gender-transformative approaches, improve outcomes for priority populations, and support the adaptation and replication of effective inclusion practices across countries. This role requires a strategic and collaborative leader who can influence across teams, partners, and geographies while balancing common standards with country-specific realities. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Provide Strategic Leadership Lead the development and implementation of the Senegal/WAEMU Gender and Inclusion Strategy. Provide strategic advice to the Country Director and Leadership Team on gender equality and inclusion priorities, risks, opportunities, and portfolio performance. Champion inclusion as a core driver of program quality, impact, and systems change across the portfolio. Promote consistent inclusion standards while supporting context-specific implementation across countries. Strengthen Inclusive Program Design and Delivery Ensure gender equality, disability inclusion, youth engagement, refugee and displaced-person inclusion, and safeguarding considerations are integrated throughout the program lifecycle. Support program teams and partners to identify and address barriers affecting participation, retention, transition to work, and dignified and fulfilling work outcomes. Guide program design, redesign, and scale-up efforts to strengthen inclusion outcomes and impact. Promote evidence-based approaches that improve outcomes for young women and other priority populations. Advance Gender Equality and Womens Economic Empowerment Lead efforts to strengthen young womens access to dignified and fulfilling work. Support partners in addressing structural barriers that limit participation and economic opportunity for young women. Promote gender-transformative programming and approaches that strengthen agency, leadership, voice, and economic inclusion. Ensure gender considerations are reflected in program strategies, implementation models, and performance frameworks. Advance Disability Inclusion, Youth Engagement and Inclusion Outcomes Strengthen the inclusion of persons with disabilities across programs and partnerships. Promote accessible and inclusive program delivery approaches. Support meaningful youth engagement by ensuring young people contribute to program design, implementation, and learning. Strengthen partnerships with youth-led organizations, organizations of persons with disabilities, and other representative institutions. Promote effective approaches to refugee and displaced-person inclusion where relevant. Drive Portfolio Learning and Performance Establish mechanisms to monitor and improve inclusion performance across the portfolio. Strengthen the use of data, evidence, and learning to inform program adaptation and decision-making. Support program teams and partners to improve inclusion-related results and accountability. Capture and share lessons, innovations, and promising practices across countries and programs. Facilitate cross-country learning and adaptation of successful inclusion approaches. Build Strong Partnerships and Influence Systems Build and maintain relationships with government, civil society, private-sector, youth-led, disability-led, and other strategic partners. Represent the Foundation in relevant external forums and networks. Promote policies, systems, and partnerships that advance gender equality and inclusion outcomes for young people. Position the Foundation as a thought leader in inclusive youth employment and economic participation. Lead and Develop a High-Performing Team Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing Gender and Inclusion team. Foster a culture of learning, collaboration, accountability, and innovation. Ensure team priorities are aligned with portfolio objectives and emerging opportunities. Support the professional development and growth of team members. WHO YOU ARE Masters degree in Gender Studies, Social Sciences, International Development, Public Policy, Human Rights, Economics, Disability Studies, or a related field. Minimum of 12 years of progressively responsible experience in gender equality, social inclusion, youth development, economic empowerment, or international development. Demonstrated experience leading complex programs or portfolios across multiple countries. Strong track record of integrating gender equality and inclusion outcomes into program design, implementation, and performance management. Experience working in one or more of the following areas: disability inclusion, youth engagement, safeguarding, refugee and displaced-person inclusion, or inclusive economic development. Deep understanding of gender-transformative programming and inclusive development approaches. Experience building the capacity of teams, partners, and stakeholders. Strong strategic thinking, stakeholder management, and influencing skills. Demonstrated ability to work across multiple country teams and partner ecosystems without direct operational authority. Strong analytical skills and ability to translate evidence into action and decision-making. Excellent verbal, written, facilitation, and presentation skills. Professional fluency in English and French is required. Demonstrates professional maturity, cultural sensitivity, humility, integrity, and alignment with Mastercard Foundations values. The Mastercard Foundation values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the organization and we are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Completion of satisfactory business references and background checks are essential conditions of employment. title: Lead, Entrepreneurship WAEMU
description: THE OPPORTUNITY Reporting to the Director of Entrepreneurship Development, WAEMU, the Program Lead, Entrepreneurship will drive execution of the Senegal/WAEMU entrepreneurship portfolio, translating the Roadmap and One Plan into high-quality delivery, partner performance, and measurable impact. The role is suited to an execution-focused leader with strong experience in entrepreneurship, MSME development, access to finance, market systems, and multi-stakeholder program delivery in West Africa. The Program Lead will align partners, internal teams, and ecosystem stakeholders; resolve delivery bottlenecks; manage risks; and use evidence and learning to strengthen results for young people, especially young women. Ideal candidates may come from development finance, impact investment, SME or inclusive finance, enterprise support, incubators and accelerators, consulting, foundations, NGOs, government enterprise agencies, or private sector organizations focused on entrepreneurship and job creation. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Program Execution and Delivery Lead delivery of the entrepreneurship portfolio against agreed outcomes, milestones, quality standards, and impact targets. Drive partner performance through clear expectations, regular performance reviews, continuous engagement, and timely course correction. Identify implementation risks early, manage delivery trade-offs, and coordinate timely mitigation actions. Apply adaptive management approaches using evidence, partner feedback, and changing market context. Technical Leadership Provide technical leadership on entrepreneurship, MSME development, inclusive finance, market systems, and enterprise growth. Advise partners on enterprise growth, investment readiness, access to finance, ecosystem strengthening, and scalable delivery models. Use market intelligence, evidence, and implementation learning to recommend portfolio improvements. Planning and Coordination Ensure effective portfolio planning, sequencing, prioritization, and resource utilization. Coordinate delivery across Foundation teams, partners, and stakeholders. Enable execution through influence, alignment, and removal of bottlenecks. Partner Stewardship and Performance Build trusted relationships with implementing partners and ecosystem actors. Establish clear expectations and monitor partner performance. Address underperformance through coaching, escalation, and agreed consequence frameworks. Portfolio Insight, Learning and Reporting Maintain visibility on portfolio performance, risks, and outcomes. Provide timely reporting and actionable recommendations. Generate evidence and insights that improve portfolio performance and decision-making. Capture, share, and apply lessons to continuously strengthen delivery and impact. WHO YOU ARE Master’s degree in Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Entrepreneurship, International Development, Public Policy, or a related field. Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience leading complex entrepreneurship, enterprise development, private sector development, inclusive finance, or market systems programs. Deep understanding of entrepreneurship ecosystems, MSME growth, access to finance, investment readiness, business development services, and job creation pathways for young people. Experience managing multi-stakeholder partnerships across West Africa, preferably with exposure to WAEMU markets and regional entrepreneurship ecosystems. Relevant experience may come from development finance institutions, impact investment or SME finance organizations, enterprise support platforms, incubators or accelerators, consulting firms, foundations, NGOs, government enterprise agencies, or private sector organizations working on entrepreneurship and job creation. Demonstrated ability to deliver results through influence, partner stewardship, strong coordination, and sound judgement rather than formal authority. Strategic and practical problem solver who can connect implementation realities with Foundation priorities, country plans, and partner delivery capacity. Excellent communicator able to translate complexity into clear action. Data-informed decision maker who uses evidence, learning, and portfolio insights to strengthen delivery, manage risk, and improve impact. Resilient, adaptable, comfortable with ambiguity, and committed to the Foundation’s values, inclusive development, and impact for young people, especially young women. The Mastercard Foundation values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the organization and we are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Completion of satisfactory business references and background checks are essential conditions of employment.
